mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth may slow.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 6.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows and unemployment rises simultaneously, it indicates an economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows and unemployment rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates stimulate economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs decrease.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are below 0.1% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation erodes corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as costs increase.
failure_condition: If inflation rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weaker demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts fall below 1 million but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment also rises, it may indicate inefficiencies in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If employment rises and unemployment increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth indicates a robust supply chain, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as production efficiency increases.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth exceeds 3% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.
